annotations.title: What does a drug's FDA or EU label say?

description: Answers what a drug's FDA label (US prescribing information) or EU summary of product characteristics (SmPC) says, today or on a past date: what it is approved for and in whom, dosage, contraindications, boxed warning, warnings, pregnancy, breastfeeding, children, older people, adverse reactions, interactions, overdose, pharmacology, storage, approval facts and the label's version history. From DailyMed and Drugs@FDA (US) and the European Commission's product information (EU). Each answer quotes the record's own words for the section, with its section number, version, effective date, SHA-256 and address; each SmPC of a product is given apart. Whether a particular use falls within the indications text is not decided here. Where the record cannot be read, matched or confirmed for the date, no text is given and the answer is unresolved, with a reason code. Not for personal dosing, timing or interaction advice, prices, shortages or news.

application.description: Optional: a US NDA, ANDA or BLA number or an EMA product number (EMEA/H/C/002677), for one authorisation.

date.description: Optional: the date asked about, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today (UTC).

medicine.description: Brand or active substance name, for example Jardiance or empagliflozin.

product.description: Optional: a strength or form as the label names it (395 mg, solution for injection), among several labels.

section.description: Optional, with topic history and since: the section (a topic name) whose change is shown.

since.description: Optional, with topic history and section: the earlier version's date, YYYY-MM-DD.

topic.description: The label section to read; approval gives the approval facts, history the versions, pharmaceutical_particulars storage and excipients.
